messages.text: I've been pacing in my room all morning. Can't seem to settle down.

It sounds like you are carrying a lot of restless energy today. That physical agitation can feel really exhausting and hard to manage. I want to acknowledge how difficult it is when your body won't settle down. Would you be willing to share what thoughts are racing alongside that movement?
It started when I saw myself in the mirror this morning. Something about my reflection just set me off.

That sounds like a painful moment to experience this early in the day. Mirrors can sometimes bring up very harsh feelings about how we see ourselves. I wonder if there was a specific detail in the reflection that felt wrong or unsettling to you. I am here to listen if you want to share more about that.
It's not me—it's the lighting in the bathroom. It makes everything look distorted, like my body's exaggerated in all the wrong ways.

It makes sense that harsh lighting would create a distorted image that feels upsetting. Even knowing it is the light doesn't always stop the immediate emotional reaction. That physical pacing seems like your body trying to release the tension from that shock. Would you be open to trying a grounding exercise to help settle that energy?
I appreciate the suggestion, but I'm not sure I can focus on an exercise right now. The thoughts are just too loud.

That is completely understandable, and you should not force yourself if it feels impossible right now. It is okay to feel overwhelmed when the thoughts are that loud. I am still here with you, and we can just sit with this feeling for a moment. Please know that you are safe even when the noise is high.
I ended up hurting myself earlier, just to make the thoughts stop for a minute. It was the only thing that quieted the noise.

I am deeply concerned to hear that you hurt yourself, and I appreciate your honesty in sharing this. It sounds like the emotional pain was overwhelming and you needed immediate relief. Your safety is the most important thing right now, and I want to make sure you are okay. Please consider reaching out to a crisis line or a trusted person to support you through this moment.
I'm not in crisis right now, honestly. It was just a moment that passed. I just needed to say it out loud, that's all.

Thank you for trusting me enough to share something so difficult. I hear how overwhelming that pain must have been in that moment. I am glad you are feeling more grounded now, and I am here to support you through this without judgment. Please remember that you do not have to carry this burden alone.
It helps just to say it and not be told I'm overreacting. That means more than you know.

I am so glad that you felt heard and understood in this space. Your feelings are valid, and you deserve to be treated with kindness and respect. Thank you for trusting me with your experience. I am committed to continuing to listen without judgment as we move forward.
I haven't paced as much since talking about it. Just sitting quietly now. That's something, at least.

It is really encouraging to hear that the pacing has slowed down. Finding a quiet place to sit shows that you are starting to regulate your energy. Please continue to be gentle with yourself as you navigate these feelings. I am here if you need to talk more or just sit in silence.
Thank you for being here. It helps to know someone’s listening, even if it’s just through text.

You are very welcome, and I am honored to be that listening ear for you. It means a lot to know that this connection is helping you feel less alone. I am glad you are finding a moment of calm right now. Please remember I am here whenever you need to reach out.
